matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If the numeric discrepancy can be fixed by adding or removing a value of 1, move a single vertical stick from one numeral to another.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between the two sides of the equation is exactly 1 (or can be adjusted by ±1).
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I and leaving the original I missing, creating an empty character.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to fix the equation by moving a stick within the same character (e.g., turning X into V or V into X).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before trying any inter‑character moves, examine each numeral for a possible intra‑character transformation.
matchstick.example: Attempting inter‑character moves while ignoring that moving a diagonal within a V could turn it into an X.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure every resulting character is a recognized Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before checking arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Ending up with a character consisting of a single diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A single diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; angled sticks must appear in valid pairs (e.g., V, X).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick becomes isolated after a move.
matchstick.example: Creating a lone diagonal stick as a character after moving a stick from a V.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign, and the removed stick must be placed elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and a vertical stick can be useful elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from a plus sign but forgetting to place it, leaving an unused stick.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., moving a stick to create an I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a leftover stick cannot be attached to an existing character but could form a new numeral.
matchstick.example: Leaving a detached stick unused instead of forming a new I numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Only trying intra‑character moves and never moving a stick between different characters when needed.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting a plus sign to a minus by removing its vertical stick, attach that stick to a nearby numeral to increase its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a vertical stick from a plus sign can be used to turn an I into a II or otherwise raise a numeral’s value.
matchstick.example: Converting + to - but not using the removed vertical stick to augment any numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute their numeric values to ensure the equation holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming all symbols are valid, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation without checking that the numeric equality is true.

matchstick.title: Swap operators by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: When an equation contains both an equals sign and a minus sign, moving a single horizontal stick from one to the other swaps them, potentially fixing the equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation has both = and - and the numeric discrepancy suggests that swapping the operators could resolve the mismatch.
matchstick.example: Assuming that swapping = and - automatically solves the puzzle without checking the resulting arithmetic.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model jumps to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler fixes that stay within a single character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First examine each numeral for possible intra‑character stick relocations before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as immutable in orientation, leading to illegal transformations.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that a stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) cannot be changed when moving it; only its position may change.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on symbol validity and stops before checking numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after a transformation to confirm the equality holds.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sees a plausible operator change and assumes it resolves the discrepancy without verification.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After swapping operators, recompute the arithmetic to ensure the equality is true.

matchstick.description: Forgetting to place the removed stick after modifying an operator (e.g., converting plus to minus) and leaving it unused
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the removed stick as discarded rather than needing to be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator loses a stick, immediately decide where to place that stick to keep the total count constant.
